info.title: governed-bi
info.summary: Corpus browsing, relationship graphs, and the turn audit surface, as JSON.
info.description:
The custom REST surface `langgraph.json` mounts at the server root, beside LangGraph Server's own routes. Spec-of-record for this surface (ADR 0007, ADR 0010).

**Most routes here are reads, and none of them serves a turn.** `POST /chat` and `POST /chat/resume` were deleted on 2026-08-18 (ADR 0014). **The return path's writes are the exception** (ADR 0015): `POST /turns/{turn_id}/raised` files an observation into `runs/feedback.sqlite`, `PATCH /observations/{id}` amends its note, and the steward's three verbs -- triage, draft a patch, withdraw one -- are mounted only when `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` is set. None of them writes graph state, none resumes a run, and **none writes to the corpus**: the write to corpus content is a human's `git commit` in a repository this process cannot reach. A turn is served by the graph `langgraph.json` mounts, over the platform's `POST /threads/{thread_id}/runs/stream`, which is not described here.

get.description:
Process liveness. Touches neither the corpus nor the database, so it answers before the session is built. Corpus status is /audit/corpus.

It used to be the one route served without a key. Since 2026-08-13 no route needs one, so it is no longer special — what still makes it the liveness probe is that it returns `{"ok": true}` and nothing else, so it reports the process's health and not that of anything the process depends on.
What this backend can do — the UI blocks on this response and adapts its affordances to it.
Assets of one type as flat rows. Omit `type` for every asset in the corpus. An unknown `type` returns an empty list, not an error.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Asset type to list. Known values: column, few_shot, join, metric, negative_example, schema, table, term. Omit for every asset; an unknown value yields an empty list.

schema.title: Response Corpus Assets Corpus Assets Get

get.description: The filterable columns of one asset type, derived from its dataclass — so a new field in the corpus schema becomes filterable with no change here and none in the UI. Also lists every known asset type.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Asset type whose columns to describe. Known values: column, few_shot, join, metric, negative_example, schema, table, term. Omit or name an unknown one and `columns` is empty with a `detail`.

get.description:
Filtered, sorted, paginated assets of one type (ADR 0009 D1).

`where` repeats as `field:op:value`, split on the first two colons only, so a value may contain them. Predicates are conjunctive. A predicate that cannot be applied is returned in `unknown_where` rather than dropped. Filtering runs over the in-memory corpus, which is what retrieval runs on (ADR 0009 D5).

Sorting always tiebreaks on `id`, so a page is stable across requests.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Asset type to list. Known values: column, few_shot, join, metric, negative_example, schema, table, term. An unknown value yields an empty page with a `detail`, not an error.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: Repeatable predicate, `field:op:value`. Split on the first two colons only, so the value may contain them. Conjunctive.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Column to sort by. Unset sorts by `id`.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `desc` reverses; any other value sorts ascending.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Clamped to >= 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Clamped to 1..500.

get.description: Lean table catalog: enough for a browser row and a badge, no prose. Fetch full detail lazily from /schema/{table_id}.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: Filter to one schema namespace.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Clamped to 1..1000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Clamped to >= 0.

get.description: One table in full, by asset id, with every column.

parameters.name: table_id
parameters.description: Table asset id.

404.description: No table asset with this id

get.description:
Every semantic-layer item touching one physical column: terms bound to it, rules on its table, FK in and out, joins whose ON clause names it, and table-grain metrics on its table.

Joins are matched by parsing the predicate, not by substring, so `id` does not match inside `customer_id`. An id that resolves to no column answers 200 with `meta.column_resolvable: false` and empty lists.

parameters.name: column_id
parameters.description: Column asset id, as carried by `columns[].id` on /schema/summary and /schema/{table_id}. Never derive one (ADR 0008 D4).

get.description:
Bounded ER view: tables as nodes, curated joins as edges (ADR 0009 D2).

`schema` and `kinds` narrow the candidate set, `focus` then walks outward over that set's edges for `radius` hops, and the budget is applied last, breadth-first from the focus — so what survives truncation is what is nearest. With no focus the budget is spent growing neighbourhoods from the best-connected node, because alphabetical order rarely holds both ends of any edge.

`boundary` and `meta` are always present. `meta.truncated` and `meta.dropped` say what was cut; a view that renders them as complete coverage is the failure this bound exists to prevent.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: Filter to one schema namespace.

parameters.name: focus
parameters.description: Table asset id to centre the neighbourhood on. Ignored when the id is outside the filtered candidate set.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: BFS hops from `focus`. No effect without one.

parameters.name: node_budget
parameters.description: Max nodes to return. Clamped to >= 1.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Comma-separated node kinds to keep. Every node here is a table, so this either keeps the graph or empties it.

get.description:
Bounded semantic graph: every asset kind as a node, edges from the reference closure. Same scope contract, `boundary` and `meta` as /graph.

Columns are not drawn; an edge touching one re-points to its owning table. Node kinds actually produced are table, join, metric, term, few_shot and negative_example.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: Filter to one schema namespace.

parameters.name: focus
parameters.description: Asset id to centre the neighbourhood on. Ignored when the id is outside the filtered candidate set.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: BFS hops from `focus`. No effect without one.

parameters.name: node_budget
parameters.description: Max nodes to return. Clamped to >= 1.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Comma-separated node kinds to keep, e.g. `table,join`.

get.description:
Served turns, newest first, out of LangGraph thread state (ADR 0014).

`thread_id` narrows to one conversation. Rows are collected per thread and then sorted by `asked_at`, because conversations interleave in time and per-thread order is not global order. `limit` counts **turns**, not threads, so the reader pages until the budget is met; it stops scanning at 1 000 threads and the response has no field that says so.

Nothing on this route authenticates (audit A7 open). `api/routes.py` names this route and `/audit/turns/{turn_id}/trace` as exactly what that costs: together they hand every thread's SQL, the full turn records and an absolute path to the conversation store to anything that can reach the port. `thread_id` narrows what one request returns and withholds nothing, because the unnarrowed read is available to the same caller. The absolute store path is this route's `meta.log_dir`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max rows. Clamped to >= 1.

parameters.name: thread_id
parameters.description: Narrow to one conversation.

get.description:
One recorded turn's record, grouped by the stage that owns each field. Found by scanning thread state; an unknown turn_id answers 200 with `found: false`, not 404.

Nothing on this route authenticates (audit A7 open). `api/routes.py` names this route and `/audit/turns` as exactly what that costs: together they hand every thread's SQL, the full turn records and an absolute path to the conversation store to anything that can reach the port. This is the deeper half of the pair -- `/audit/turns` serves a projection of each record plus the store path in `meta.log_dir`, while this route serves one turn's record whole, every recorded field of it.

parameters.name: turn_id
parameters.description: Turn id from `record.turn_id`, as carried by /audit/turns rows and by every chat response.

get.description: Corpus inventory plus problems: content hash, asset counts, schemas, structure totals. `fatal` and `degradations` stay separate (ADR 0008 D9) and `servable` is false when any fatal problem is present.

Open questions, oldest first: unanswered `ask_user` interrupts union open `raised` notes (`from_refusal` / `wrong_answer`). Interrupt rows come from LangGraph interrupt state (ADR 0014). Raised rows come from `ServeState.raised`. Answering an interrupt from here would resume a thread the operator was not the one asked (ADR 0006 B9) and is still refused.

**Two walks of the thread store per request.** Interrupts are read with `status=interrupted`, a handful of threads at any volume. Notes are filed on *finished* turns, so that walk sends **no** status filter at all: a thread sits in `idle`, in `error` after a crashed run, or in `busy` while a later question runs, and filtering on `idle` hid a filed note for as long as it sat elsewhere -- permanently under `error`, which nothing moves a thread out of. So no note is hidden by its thread's status; the price is that the note walk projects `values.raised` off every thread in the store, up to 20 pages of 50, uncached, per request.

`meta.truncated` is load-bearing (ADR 0009) and covers three losses without saying which: the page window, and either walk stopping on the 1000-thread bound. Both walks sort `updated_at` ascending, so past that bound the threads dropped are the most recently touched and the newest note is the first one missing -- `truncated` is the only signal that it happened. `meta.threads_scanned` is the count of **distinct** threads read across both walks (a paused thread is fetched twice and counted once); it distinguishes an empty queue from a store that was not read, and it now spans the whole store rather than only the paused conversations.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max rows. Rejected outside 1..500.

post.summary: File an observation about a finished turn
post.description: Files into `runs/feedback.sqlite` (ADR 0015). Was an append onto the `ServeState.raised` checkpoint channel, which is why it used to 409 on a paused thread -- the write would have consumed the live `ask_user` interrupt. **That 409 is gone, deliberately**: nothing writes graph state, and the reader whose turn is paused is the one most likely to want to complain. Nothing here authenticates, so any caller reaching the port can file against any turn; that was true before and is unchanged.

category.description: Optional refinement of `kind`. The first tap files something valid; a refinement is never a gate. Refused with 422 when it cannot apply to the card `kind` names.

expected.description: What the answer should have been, at most 200 characters. Asked for **after** filing succeeds, so it is a bonus rather than a gate -- a note that blocks submission is a note nobody writes.

404.description: Turn not found, or the envelope has no thread_id, or the thread the turn names is not in the store (`ThreadNotFound`). `detail` is a sentence, not a list.

422.description: **Two different bodies under one status.** The handler's own rejections -- an unknown `kind`, or a `note` longer than 4000 characters after stripping -- raise `HTTPException` and so answer `HTTPError`, whose `detail` is a string that names the limit; both are checked before the turn is read, so a rejected note never reaches the writer. FastAPI's own request validation (a body that is not a JSON object, or absent) answers `HTTPValidationError`, whose `detail` is a **list**. A client must handle both shapes on this status.

201.description: Filed. **201 and not 200**: the route creates a row in a store rather than appending to a channel, and a client should not have to read the body to learn which.

get.description: Oldest first, because the row that has waited longest is the one to act on. Sorting by cluster size instead would make the long tail permanently invisible. Ties inside one second break by insertion order, not by id -- an id carries a random suffix, and an importer files 73 rows in the same second. Nothing here authenticates, so any caller reaching the port reads every open question, and those questions can name assets. That was accepted on the grounds that `/audit/turns` already discloses every thread's SQL to the same caller.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Comma-separated. Declared: `open`, `triaged`, `declined`, `duplicate`, `addressed`, `blocked_on_a_person`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: One category. 422 names the declared set.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: `cluster` returns `clusters` instead of `rows`. Any other value is ignored rather than refused, because a client that mistypes a grouping should still see the queue.

200.description: One page, in one of two shapes.

422.description: An undeclared `state` or `category`. `detail` names the declared set.

get.summary: One observation, its patches and its history
get.description: `derived_state` is null on every patch: this route has no session and cannot read the corpus. `tools/check_landed.py` is what answers landing, from the corpus.

200.description: The row, its patches and its transitions.

patch.summary: Amend the note on an untriaged observation
patch.description: The one mutable field outside the lifecycle, and it earns that by being the field the design asks for **after** filing succeeds -- a note that gates submission is a note nobody writes. **Freezes at `triaged`**: a reviewer reading a row whose text changes underneath them is worse than a second observation. No transition is recorded, because nothing about the row's state changed.

expected.description: Folded into the note as an `expected:` line rather than stored separately, because it is one claim about one turn.

409.description: Somebody has already triaged it, so the note is frozen. `detail` says which state it is in.

422.description: The note or the expected line is over its cap.

post.summary: Move an observation to a triaged state
post.description: The transition table decides what is legal, not the handler: a move it does not declare is 409, which is how a queue avoids acquiring a row nothing can move on from. The fields a state makes mandatory -- `decline_reason` on a decline, `blocked_note` on a block -- are enforced by the same validator that enforces them at filing. **Mounted only when `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` is set, and 404 otherwise** -- a 403 would confirm the route exists. This is a deployment switch and not an identity: `api/auth.py` returns one principal, so with the switch on, whoever reaches the port is the steward. The honest control is that it is off.

200.description: The moved row and its history.

404.description: No such observation, or the router is not mounted.

409.description: The transition table does not declare this move.

422.description: An undeclared `to` or `decline_reason`, or a field the target state makes mandatory and the body omits. `detail` is a list on the validator's rejections.

post.description: Records what a change to the corpus would be. **It does not write to the corpus and cannot**: the only write is a human's `git commit` in a repository this process cannot reach, which is the provenance gate the design is. `tools/export_bundle.py` turns this row into a diff. **Mounted only when `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` is set, and 404 otherwise** -- a 403 would confirm the route exists. This is a deployment switch and not an identity: `api/auth.py` returns one principal, so with the switch on, whoever reaches the port is the steward. The honest control is that it is off.

intent.description: `new_asset` is **declared and not draftable**: `corpus/patch.py` has no create primitive, so no tool can carry it and the store refuses it at the draft rather than at the handoff. The member stays because a create primitive would want the name.

asset_type.description: Required on the intents that author an asset.

was.description: The field's current text. Enforced when the edit is applied.

base_corpus_content_hash.description: The **full** digest. A 16-character prefix is refused, because it never equals what the landing check compares it against.

observations.description: The observations this answers. May be empty. Each must exist -- a patch attached to nothing is a patch the queue can never surface.

404.description: An observation in `observations` does not exist, or the router is not mounted.

422.description: An undeclared enum member, a missing `namespace`, a truncated corpus hash, or any rule in `feedback/validate.py`. `detail` is a list on the validator's rejections and a string on the handler's.

get.description: No landing state on this route, deliberately: landing is answered by reading the corpus, which this process does at load time and not per request. A stale `landed_*` here would disagree with `tools/check_landed.py` -- two answers to one question. **Mounted only when `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` is set, and 404 otherwise** -- a 403 would confirm the route exists. This is a deployment switch and not an identity: `api/auth.py` returns one principal, so with the switch on, whoever reaches the port is the steward. The honest control is that it is off.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Comma-separated. Declared: `draft`, `exported`, `withdrawn`.

422.description: An undeclared `state`. `detail` names the declared set.

post.summary: Abandon a patch, with a reason
post.description: Legal from `draft` and from `exported` both -- a bundle that went out and was rejected in review is the common case, and leaving it `exported` forever is the unclosable row this design exists to remove. The reason is required: a terminal state whose why lives only in somebody's memory is a patch that gets re-drafted from scratch six weeks later. **Mounted only when `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` is set, and 404 otherwise** -- a 403 would confirm the route exists. This is a deployment switch and not an identity: `api/auth.py` returns one principal, so with the switch on, whoever reaches the port is the steward. The honest control is that it is off.

404.description: No such patch, or the router is not mounted.

409.description: `PATCH_TRANSITIONS` does not declare this move -- withdrawing an already withdrawn patch, for instance.

422.description: No reason, or a rule in `feedback/validate.py`.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: Null on an asset kind that carries no namespace.

provenance_status.title: Provenance Status
provenance_status.description: Null means not measured, which is not the same as clean (ADR 0005 §6).

by_type.title: By Type
by_type.description: Count per asset_type, key-sorted. A type with no assets is absent.

fatal.title: Fatal
fatal.description: Problems that make the corpus unservable.

degradations.title: Degradations
degradations.description: Problems the corpus is served despite. Kept apart from `fatal` (ADR 0008 D9).

corpus_content_hash.title: Corpus Content Hash
corpus_content_hash.description: Digest of the served corpus tree. The treatment identity of any measurement taken against this server.

schemas.title: Schemas
schemas.description: Sorted distinct schema namespaces over the loaded table assets.

servable.title: Servable
servable.description: False when any fatal problem is present.

join_edges.title: Join Edges
join_edges.description: Distinct ordered table pairs carrying a join.

references.title: References
references.description: Assets that reference at least one other asset.

found.title: Found
found.description: False when no logged turn carries this turn_id. `turn_id` is then the only other key.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: How the turn ended: one of `answered`, `refused`, `clarification`, `capped`, `crashed`, `no_sql` (`register/stages.py::Outcome`). Not enumerated in this schema because the handler passes the recorded string through. **`no_sql` was added on 2026-08-18** for a turn that ended having executed no governed statement; turns recorded before that date carry `answered` for the same state, so a list spanning the boundary mixes two taxonomies (ADR 0006 §5).

stages.title: Stages
stages.description: Every register field grouped by owning stage, in register/stages.Stage order; stages the register does not name sort last, alphabetically.

clarifications.title: Clarifications
clarifications.description:
What this turn asked its reader mid-flight and what they answered: one object per `ask_user` call, `{clarification_id, question, why, answer, turn_id, basis, deferred, resolution}`. Empty when the turn asked nothing, which is a read and not a shrug — the reader read the channel either way.

**Added 2026-08-19.** The `clarifications` channel had two writers and no reader, so a turn whose SQL a *person* selected showed no sign of having asked. Read beside the envelope and not joined into it: `get_turn` returns the five keys the record node stored, and a test holds it to them. The unanswered half of the same pair is `GET /clarifications/pending`.

ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.description: `record.execution.attempts` — one row per SQL attempt. Empty when the turn attempted none.

missing_required.title: Missing Required
missing_required.description: Sorted names of required register fields this record does not carry. Judged against today's register, not the one in force when the turn was logged.

undeclared_keys.title: Undeclared Keys
undeclared_keys.description: Sorted record keys the register does not declare.

observations.title: Observations
observations.description: Observations filed about this turn, read from `runs/feedback.sqlite` keyed on `turn_id`. Was `raised`, which read the deleted checkpoint channel. On the trace for the same reason `clarifications` is: somebody read the statement above and said it was wrong, so a trace without it shows half of what happened.

AuditTraceResponse.title: AuditTraceResponse
AuditTraceResponse.description: One logged turn, its record split by the stage that owns each field. Every key beyond `found` and `turn_id` is present only when `found` is true.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: How the turn ended: one of `answered`, `refused`, `clarification`, `capped`, `crashed`, `no_sql` (`register/stages.py::Outcome`). Not enumerated in this schema because the handler passes the recorded string through. **`no_sql` was added on 2026-08-18** for a turn that ended having executed no governed statement; turns recorded before that date carry `answered` for the same state, so a list spanning the boundary mixes two taxonomies (ADR 0006 §5).

latency_sec.title: Latency Sec
latency_sec.description: Seconds, unrounded. **Not reachable as an absence on a served turn**: `wrap_node` stamps `turn_started_at`, so only a hand-built state is unmeasured. The old `string` member of this union came from the JSONL log’s `json.dumps(..., default=str)`, which is deleted with the log (ADR 0014); an unmeasured `Measured` now survives the checkpoint as itself (`register/quantity.py`) and would reach the wire as an object, which `ui/lib/schemas.ts` validates as `z.number().nullable()` and would reject. Narrowed to match the client rather than documenting a shape nothing produces.

incomplete_fields.title: Incomplete Fields
incomplete_fields.description: How many required register fields this record is missing, judged against today's register.

AuditTurnSummaryResponse.title: AuditTurnSummaryResponse
AuditTurnSummaryResponse.description: One row of the turn list. The record-sourced keys are exactly api/thread_turns.SUMMARY_FIELDS: turn_id, run_id, thread_id, question_id, db_id, outcome, terminal_reason, schemas, generated_sql, latency_sec, execution.

n.title: N
n.description: Rows returned, after the limit and any thread_id filter.

log_dir.title: Log Dir
log_dir.description: Absolute path the turns were read from. Since ADR 0014 that is the conversation checkpoint database (a file), not a directory of logs. The key is unchanged so the client's footer keeps rendering.

question.title: Question
question.description: **Nullable, and it was declared non-nullable until 2026-08-22.** On an interrupt row the handler passes `value.get("question")` straight through (`api/thread_turns.py::_open_questions_of`), so a clarification interrupt whose payload carries no `question` key reaches the wire as null. Raised notes always carry a string -- the note, or a fixed sentence naming the kind.

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: **Nullable, and it was declared non-nullable until 2026-08-22.** Both walks pass `thread.get("thread_id")` through unchanged (`api/thread_turns.py::_open_questions_of` and `::_open_raised_of`), so a thread row that arrives without the field reaches the wire as null rather than being dropped.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: `data_definition` or `ranking_ambiguity` on interrupt rows; null on raised notes.

interrupt_id.title: Interrupt Id
interrupt_id.description: **On the wire but not in `meta.columns`, and absent rather than null on half the rows.** `api/thread_turns.py::_open_questions_of` adds `item.get("id")` to every interrupt row -- so the key is present there, and null if the platform's `Interrupt` carried no id -- while `::_open_raised_of` omits it entirely, because a finished refusal names no resume. So a client must tell absent from null here, which is the opposite of the rule the declared columns follow. Added to this schema on 2026-08-22; the field itself predates it.

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: The key of the thread's `interrupts` mapping (`{task_id: [Interrupt, ...]}`), so a JSON object key and never null. **Absent on raised-note rows**, same as `interrupt_id`. Together the two are what a resume would have to name; this surface carries them and does not use them -- answering from here is refused (ADR 0006 B9) until the corpus write path has a provenance gate.

observation_id.description: The observation this row came from, or null on an interrupt row. `observation_id` since 2026-08-23, where it was `report_id`: that name was minted by the deleted `serve/raised.py`, and report would have been the third meaning of the word in one system. Declared and null-where-inapplicable rather than absent, so a client never has to tell no-value from no-such-key.

PendingClarificationRowResponse.title: PendingClarificationRowResponse
PendingClarificationRowResponse.description:
One row of the pending queue, unioned from two populations: an unanswered `ask_user` interrupt and an open `raised` note.

**Two rules, and they differ.** The nine columns `PENDING_FIELDS` declares are *always present*, null where they do not apply -- `clarification_id`/`basis` on every note, `report_id` on every interrupt -- because a client forced to tell "no value" from "no such key" ends up guessing which kind of row it holds. `interrupt_id` and `task_id` are *carried* rather than declared, and are genuinely absent on a note. `source` says which kind of row this is and is the one column never null.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True when this page is not everything: more rows than the window returned, or a walk that stopped on the 1000-thread bound. A silently short list reads as everything (ADR 0009).

threads_scanned.title: Threads Scanned
threads_scanned.description: Distinct threads read to build this page, across both walks -- the whole store, not only the interrupted ones, and not a count of reads. Distinguishes an empty queue from a store that was not scanned.

on.title: On
on.description: The join predicate. Empty when the edge declares none.

BoundaryEdgeResponse.title: BoundaryEdgeResponse
BoundaryEdgeResponse.description: A curated join leaving the scope for another namespace, as a navigable stub. One stub per (in-scope table, far table), whatever the number of joins between them.

CapabilitiesModelsResponse.title: CapabilitiesModelsResponse
CapabilitiesModelsResponse.description: The three model surfaces this run resolved, for the settings page (`api/routes.py::models_for`). All three keys are always present -- the function returns a literal three-key mapping -- so a surface with nothing resolved arrives as three nulls rather than as an absent key.

can_edit.title: Can Edit
can_edit.description: Always false: this server has no corpus write route. The corpus is edited in its own repository through review and a pinned hash.

edit_mode.title: Edit Mode
edit_mode.description: Always "none", for the same reason as can_edit.

has_live_model.title: Has Live Model
has_live_model.description: False when no agent model is configured; the graph still runs and refuses.

model.title: Model
model.description: Resolved agent model id, from `knobs_resolved.chat_model` (`api/routes.py::capabilities_for`). **Not `llm_model`**, which this description named until 2026-08-22 and which `register/knobs.py` has never declared -- the string survives only inside other knobs' description text, so a client written from the old sentence went looking for a knob that does not exist. Same value as `models.agent.id`; kept as a top-level field because the header chip reads it.

can_clarify.title: Can Clarify
can_clarify.description: Clarification needs both the streaming transport and a live model.

checkpoint_durable.title: Checkpoint Durable
checkpoint_durable.description: Whether this deployment mounts a durable checkpointer. **Derived** from `langgraph.json` — `checkpointer.path` names a module and factory, and that module is on disk — so the flag goes false if either stops existing, without anyone editing a line (ADR 0009 D4). It is honest about being a *configuration reading* and not an observation: the platform injects the saver into the graph it runs and this custom app never holds that graph, so there is no live handle here to ask. Reported as the literal `False` until 2026-08-18, when `POST /chat`'s process-local `InMemorySaver` — the thing that comment described — was deleted (ADR 0014). Audit A10, `docs/open-work.md` §4.4.

hitl_survives_process_restart.title: Hitl Survives Process Restart
hitl_survives_process_restart.description:
Whether a clarification paused at `interrupt()` survives a restart of this process. Reads the same derivation as `checkpoint_durable`, and cannot be true while that is false: an `ask_user` interrupt *is* checkpoint state, and the resume reads it back out of the same store through the platform's `Command(resume=…)`, so this is one observation and not two.

**The behaviour was watched end to end on 2026-08-19**: a turn paused at `ask_user`, the process was killed and confirmed off the port, a fresh process re-mounted the prompt from checkpointed state, and answering it resumed the turn to a correct answer. So the flag is no longer derived from nothing. It is still derived from configuration rather than re-checked per process, which is what remains open. Audit A10, `docs/open-work.md` §4.4.

CapabilitiesResponse.title: CapabilitiesResponse
CapabilitiesResponse.description: What this server can actually do. The UI blocks on it, so every key is always present.

id.title: Id
id.description: The model id, read out of `knobs_resolved` rather than off the live client, so the settings page shows the identity a run is actually recorded under. `agent.id` is the `chat_model` knob and `utility.id` is `llm_utility_model`. Null when nothing resolved one -- an offline profile with no model wired.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Which gateway served the id (`llm_provider` / `llm_utility_provider`). Carried beside the id and never folded into it: the same id behind two gateways is two treatments. Both knobs default to `openai`, so this is null only when `knobs_resolved` carries no entry at all.

effort.title: Effort
effort.description: Reasoning effort in the engine's vocabulary. `agent.effort` is the `llm_reasoning_effort` knob; `utility.effort` is **observed off the live client** by `model/provider.py::reasoning_effort_of`, because the register declares no utility-effort knob. Null means either no live utility client or a client that sends no reasoning configuration -- a real state, not a failure to look.

ModelSurfaceResponse.title: ModelSurfaceResponse
ModelSurfaceResponse.description: One chat surface's resolved identity (`api/routes.py::models_for`). Every field is present and every field is nullable.

id.title: Id
id.description: The `embedding_model` knob, **provider-qualified** (`bedrock:amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`) and reported verbatim. Do not split it on `:` -- the qualifier is part of the vector cache-key identity (`retrieve.semantic.cache_key` is `model|dimensions|text`) and the id itself can contain a colon, so parsing it corrupts the one field that keeps two gateways' vectors apart.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: The `embedding_provider` knob, carried beside the qualified id rather than parsed out of it.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.description: The `embedding_dimensions` knob -- the served width, probed off the embedder (`model/embedder.py` records `int(embedder.dimensions)`) rather than declared. Null when no embedder resolved.

EmbeddingSurfaceResponse.title: EmbeddingSurfaceResponse
EmbeddingSurfaceResponse.description: The embedding surface (`api/routes.py::models_for`). Same three-key shape as a chat surface, with `dimensions` where a chat surface carries `effort`.

dialect.title: Dialect
dialect.description: Always present: every connector declares one, and the handler falls back to `postgres` for a partial session.

host.title: Host
host.description: **Absent, not null**, when the connector's endpoint does not carry one -- SQLite is a file, and Postgres omits any DSN field it could not parse. `datasource/postgres.py::endpoint` stringifies every value it emits.

port.title: Port
port.description: A **string**, not a number: `datasource/postgres.py::endpoint` emits `str(value)` for host, port and database alike. Absent for SQLite and for an unparseable DSN.

database.title: Database
database.description: The database name, or for SQLite the file name rather than the absolute path. Absent when the endpoint does not carry one.

ConnectionResponse.title: ConnectionResponse
ConnectionResponse.description: Which warehouse this engine is pointed at (`api/routes.py::connection_for`), **credential-free by construction**: the redaction lives in the connector that owns the DSN (`datasource/postgres.py::endpoint`), which never parses `user` or `password` out at all, so there is no field here for a caller to leak. Only `dialect` is guaranteed -- the other three are whatever `connector.endpoint` returned, and an unparseable DSN returns an empty mapping.

table_id.title: Table Id
table_id.description: Empty when the id did not resolve.

column_resolvable.title: Column Resolvable
column_resolvable.description: False when the id names no column asset. Every list above is then empty and the status is still 200.

joins.title: Joins
joins.description: Joins whose ON clause names this column, matched by parsing the predicate.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: Metrics based on this column's table.

id.title: Id
id.description: The column's asset id. Callers must never derive one (ADR 0008 D4).

description.title: Description
description.description: The column body, falling back to its summary.

references.title: References
references.description: Asset id of the column this one points at.

id.title: Id
id.description: The column's asset id. Callers must never derive one (ADR 0008 D4).

name.title: Name
name.description: Dataclass field name; also the left-hand side of a `where` triple.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: api/browse.FieldKind. Decides which operators the field offers.

ops.title: Ops
ops.description: Operators accepted for this field. Anything else lands in `unknown_where` and is not applied.

sortable.title: Sortable
sortable.description: False for block and list kinds.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: The register names this field as the type's identifier.

type.title: Type
type.description: Echoed back; null when the request named none or an unknown one.

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: Derived from the asset dataclass, so a new field becomes filterable with no change here. Empty when `type` is null.

types.title: Types
types.description: Every asset type the register knows, sorted.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Why `columns` is empty. Present only when the request named no type or an unknown one; a known type omits the key entirely.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: One flat object per asset: every dataclass field plus `asset_type`. Enums render as their value, lists as lists of text, nested blocks as their rendered text or null.

total.title: Total
total.description: Matching assets after filtering, before pagination.

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: The same column set /corpus/fields returns for this type.

unknown_where.title: Unknown Where
unknown_where.description: Predicates that were **not** applied — unknown field, unsupported operator, or a malformed triple. Reported rather than dropped, so a filtered-looking list is never silently unfiltered.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Why the result is empty. Present only when `type` names no known asset type.

n_nodes.title: N Nodes
n_nodes.description: Nodes in this response, after the budget.

n_edges.title: N Edges
n_edges.description: Edges in this response — both endpoints kept.

n_total_nodes.title: N Total Nodes
n_total_nodes.description: Nodes in the whole graph, before any scope.

n_matched_nodes.title: N Matched Nodes
n_matched_nodes.description: Nodes the scope selected, before the budget.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: The budget cut nodes the scope had selected.

node_budget.title: Node Budget
node_budget.description: The budget as applied, after clamping to >= 1.

GraphMetaResponse.title: GraphMetaResponse
GraphMetaResponse.description: What the view cut. `truncated` and `dropped` are load-bearing: a view that silently renders 120 of 656 nodes reads as complete coverage (ADR 0009 D2).

kinds.title: Kinds
kinds.description: Sorted, or null when none were requested.

GraphScopeResponse.title: GraphScopeResponse
GraphScopeResponse.description: The scope **as applied**, complete. The client compares it field-for-field against what it asked for and re-scopes when they differ, so every key is always present.

relation.title: Relation
relation.description: Labelled from the source asset's kind: join, measures (metric), grounds (term), exemplifies (few_shot), belongs_to (column), has_column (table); anything else is "related".

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The asset type. Columns are not drawn; their edges re-point to the owning table.

label.title: Label
label.description: physical_name, else name, else the id.

provenance_status.title: Provenance Status
provenance_status.description: Null means not measured, which is not the same as clean (ADR 0005 §6).

edges.title: Edges
edges.description: Only edges with both endpoints kept.

other_table_id.title: Other Table Id
other_table_id.description: Whichever endpoint is not this column's table.

granularity.title: Granularity
granularity.description: Always "table": only table-grain metrics are listed.

id.title: Id
id.description: ``<table_id>#rule-<index>``. Positional: table rules are strings, not assets.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: Always null: a rule string carries none.

provenance_status.title: Provenance Status
provenance_status.description: Always null, for the same reason.

id.title: Id
id.description: The first join asset's id, else ``<source>-><target>``.

on.title: On
on.description: The first join's predicate; empty when it declares none.

join_ids.title: Join Ids
join_ids.description: Every join asset on this table pair.

n_relationships.title: N Relationships
n_relationships.description: Distinct ON digests among `join_ids` — a bidirectional declaration is one relationship, not two.

label.title: Label
label.description: physical_name, falling back to the id.

has_suspect.title: Has Suspect
has_suspect.description: Any column of this table is marked suspect.

edges.title: Edges
edges.description: Only edges with both endpoints kept.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: Empty string when the table carries no namespace.

description.title: Description
description.description: The table body, falling back to its summary.

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: In the table's declared column order.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: Empty string when the table carries no namespace.

value.title: Value
value.description: The recorded value, or null when absent.

present.title: Present
present.description: The key is in the record and its value is not null.

required_and_absent.title: Required And Absent
required_and_absent.description: The register requires this field and the record does not carry it — the turn is not quotable.

why.title: Why
why.description: The register's stated reason the field exists.

TurnRecord.title: TurnRecord
TurnRecord.description:
The turn record: exactly the 38 keys register/record.record_keys() declares, projected by serve/nodes/stamp.py — attempt_id, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, context_hash, corpus_content_hash, crossings, db_id, delivery_hash, error_type, evicted, execution, facet_channels, facet_degraded, facet_hits, failed_stage, generated_sql, guard, guardrail_errors, knobs_resolved, latency_sec, lexical_coverage, licensed, n_re_served, negative, outcome, prompt_set_hash, pulled_in, question_id, reflect_verdict, rewrite, run_id, schema_ranking, schemas, terminal_reason, thread_id, tool_delivered, turn_id, usage.

An empty object on a paused (clarification) turn and on a request a chat route rejected. A quantity the turn could not measure is an object ``{state, raw, why, relation}`` rather than a number, so `not measured` never renders as 0.

ObservationResponse.title: ObservationResponse
ObservationResponse.description: One row of `runs/feedback.sqlite`'s `observation` table (ADR 0015). Replaces `RaisedRowResponse`, which described a row on the deleted `ServeState.raised` checkpoint channel. Two differences matter to a client: the id field is `observation_id` and not `report_id`, and `open` is **computed** from `state` rather than stored -- a row cannot be open and terminal, because there is no column that could disagree with the state. **The projection is narrowed for an unauthenticated caller.** `gold_sql`, `gold_fingerprint` and `pred_fingerprint` are the held-out benchmark's reference answer and its comparison fingerprints; conformance rule V12 exists to keep a held-out question out of the corpus, and serving the answer over HTTP would be the same contamination with the gate bypassed. They are omitted unless `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` is set. What stays public -- `question`, `generated_sql`, `licensed`, `missing_tables` -- is what makes a row reviewable, and `/audit/turns/{turn_id}/trace` already discloses a turn's SQL to the same caller.

observation_id.description: `obs-{yyyymmddThhmmssZ}-{8hex}`, minted server-side. The join key the pending queue and the trace read a row back by.

source.description: Which population filed it. `eval` means an eval artifact rather than a person, and it is the only value on which `question_is_held_out` is true.

kind.description: Unchanged from the deleted route, so a client written against it keeps working. The refinement is `category`.

category.description: The reader's refinement or the importer's derivation. Null is legal: the first tap may be all there is, and a category nobody chose beats one somebody guessed.

state.description: Stored. Every member is moved by a named actor; there is no `closed`, because nothing would branch on it.

open.description: **Computed**, never stored: `state not in {declined, duplicate}`. `addressed` is open, because a patch exists and until it lands nothing the filer cared about has changed.

note.description: Free text, stripped, capped at 4000 characters.

decline_reason.description: Required on a decline and null everywhere else. The reason *is* the notification: there is no declined badge without a sentence.

blocked_note.description: Required on `blocked_on_a_person`, and the whole content of that state -- there is nobody to escalate to, so the sentence is what a reader gets.

turn_id.description: Null on an imported observation: an eval artifact carries no turn id on any row, and a synthesised one would 404 on `/audit/turns/{id}/trace`.

question.description: Copied from the turn, not joined to it: the turn record elides after 25 turns, so a join returns nothing six months from now -- which is when a reviewer reads the queue.

licensed.description: The table allowlist Layer 6 enforced against on that turn.

missing_tables.description: Gold tables the turn was **not** allowed to read. The defect itself rather than a symptom, and empty on an operator-filed row -- there is no reference statement to diff against.

gold_sql.description: Present only on an imported observation. The falsifiable claim on such a row, and stronger than a sentence: it is compared by fingerprint. **Present only for the steward.** The reader routes mount unauthenticated, so this field is omitted unless the engine was started with `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` set -- the same switch that mounts the steward's verbs, read once. A client must treat it as absent, not null.

gold_fingerprint.description: **Present only for the steward.** The reader routes mount unauthenticated, so this field is omitted unless the engine was started with `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` set -- the same switch that mounts the steward's verbs, read once. A client must treat it as absent, not null.

pred_fingerprint.description: **Present only for the steward.** The reader routes mount unauthenticated, so this field is omitted unless the engine was started with `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` set -- the same switch that mounts the steward's verbs, read once. A client must treat it as absent, not null.

question_is_held_out.description: **A warning and not metadata.** True when the question came from the held-out split, which is every imported row. A person who writes corpus prose from one contaminates the benchmark, and conformance rule V12 is the gate; this field is what tells the reader before they read.

patches.description: Candidate corpus changes drafted for this observation. `derived_state` is null on this route: answering whether one landed needs the loaded corpus, and this route has no session.

history.description: Every transition, oldest first, each carrying the actor that moved it. The append-only audit trail.

ObservationAcceptedResponse.title: ObservationAcceptedResponse
ObservationAcceptedResponse.description: The 201 envelope. The row is under `observation`, not at the top level.

QueueMeta.title: QueueMeta
QueueMeta.description: What the rows alone cannot say. `truncated` is load-bearing (ADR 0009): a caller that cannot tell a full page from the end of the queue stops at the first page and believes it saw everything.

total.description: Rows behind the filter, ignoring the page.

grouped.description: Clusters in this page. Present only under `group=cluster`.

PatchResponse.title: PatchResponse
PatchResponse.description: One row of the `patch` table (ADR 0015 §4). A patch records what a change to the corpus *would* be; it is never the change. The write is a human's `git commit` in the corpus repository, which this process cannot reach -- that gap is the provenance gate the design exists for, so no field here says a patch was applied. **Landing is derived** by reading the corpus (`tools/check_landed.py`) and appears on this shape only as `derived_state`, which is null on every route that has no corpus loaded. **The projection is narrowed for an unauthenticated caller.** `was`, `becomes`, `rationale` and `base_corpus_content_hash` are the steward's working draft and are omitted unless `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` is set. The *existence* of a patch is not withheld -- its text is. `GET /patches` 404s under the same switch, and until 2026-08-23 this shape served the same content through `GET /observations/{observation_id}` regardless, which is a 404 on one door and an open window on the other.

author.description: Who drafted it. `operator` on everything this route creates.

intent.description: What the patch is for. **Two members author no asset on purpose**: an `exclusion_request` is an argument a human transcribes by hand, because exclusion is enforced by the absence of a tool; `engine_defect` and `no_change` record that the corpus is not at fault. Only `edit_asset` produces a bundle. `new_asset` is **declared and not draftable**: `corpus/patch.py` has no create primitive, so no tool can carry it and the store refuses it at the draft rather than at the handoff. The member stays because a create primitive would want the name.

state.description: Stored. `exported` means a bundle is on disk and is terminal from the store's point of view -- what happens next happens in a git repository. `withdrawn` requires a reason.

namespace.description: The schema the change is in.

rationale.description: Why, in the drafter's words. **Present only for the steward.** The reader routes mount unauthenticated, so this field is omitted unless the engine was started with `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` set -- the same switch that mounts the steward's verbs, read once. A client must treat it as absent, not null.

asset_type.description: Null on the intents that author no asset.

asset_id.description: Null on the intents that author no asset.

field_path.description: `summary` or `body`, and nothing else. The editable set is enforced in `corpus/patch.py`: a governance, provenance, audit or columns field is refused.

was.description: The field's text when the patch was drafted. **Enforced at apply time** -- if the corpus no longer holds this, the edit is refused rather than merged. **Present only for the steward.** The reader routes mount unauthenticated, so this field is omitted unless the engine was started with `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` set -- the same switch that mounts the steward's verbs, read once. A client must treat it as absent, not null.

becomes.description: The replacement text. **Present only for the steward.** The reader routes mount unauthenticated, so this field is omitted unless the engine was started with `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` set -- the same switch that mounts the steward's verbs, read once. A client must treat it as absent, not null.

base_corpus_content_hash.description: The full 64-character digest of the corpus the patch was authored against. A truncated prefix -- which is what every display shows -- is refused with 422, because it never equals the digest the landing check compares it against and the patch would report `superseded` while nothing had changed. **Present only for the steward.** The reader routes mount unauthenticated, so this field is omitted unless the engine was started with `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` set -- the same switch that mounts the steward's verbs, read once. A client must treat it as absent, not null.

expected_corpus_content_hash.description: Null until a bundle is built, because it is the hash of a tree nobody has written yet. A hash-shaped string nobody can compare is worse than an absence.

ladder.description: Tier name to that tier's result, as the store holds it. Open-ended because the surface renders whatever tiers ran rather than a fixed three.

observations.description: The observations this patch answers. May be empty: a patch drafted from a corpus audit rather than from a failure answers nobody, and refusing it would push that work outside the store where nothing records it.

derived_state.description: **Derived, never stored**, and null wherever the route has no corpus loaded. One of `handed_off`, `landed_verified`, `landed_matched`, `retrieval_verified`, `superseded`.

ObservationCluster.title: ObservationCluster
ObservationCluster.description: Observations grouped by `(category, schema)` and nothing else. **The grouping is structural, and a client must say so**: nothing read the questions and decided they mean the same thing. Measured on the 73 imported coverage misses the largest cluster is 3 and 49% of rows are in a cluster at all -- which answers ADR 0015's open question 7 with a negative result, so a caller should treat this as an optional grouping over a list rather than as the primary shape.

category.description: Null when the members carry no category.

schema.description: The namespace the members are about.

n_distinct_questions.description: Distinct question texts among the members. Lower than `n` means the same question was filed more than once, which is a different fact from a cluster of related failures.

shared_missing_tables.description: Tables absent from every member's licensed set. Evidence, and deliberately **not** part of the key: 56 of the 73 miss exactly one table and those tables are mostly different, so the absence identifies a turn rather than a problem.

ObservationQueueResponse.title: ObservationQueueResponse
ObservationQueueResponse.description: One page of the queue, in one of **two shapes under one operation**: `rows` by default, `clusters` under `group=cluster`. Exactly one of the two is present, which is why neither is required here.

ObservationDetailResponse.title: ObservationDetailResponse
ObservationDetailResponse.description: One observation, the patches drafted against it, and its transition history. The same shape the 201 envelope's `observation` carries, which is why a client needs one parser.

patches.description: `derived_state` is null on every row: this route has no session, so it cannot read the corpus, and answering "did this land" from an empty corpus view would say `superseded` about everything.

entity.description: Which table the row is about. The transition log is one table for both, so a client reading a history has to be told which entity moved.

from_state.description: Null on the row that filed it.

moved_by.description: The role the transition table declares, not an identity. On this deployment one person holds all three.

detail.description: Free text the steward typed when moving the row. **Present only for the steward.** The reader routes mount unauthenticated, so this field is omitted unless the engine was started with `GOVERNED_BI_FEEDBACK_ADMIN` set -- the same switch that mounts the steward's verbs, read once. A client must treat it as absent, not null.

history.description: Append-only. Who moved it, in order.

PatchEnvelope.title: PatchEnvelope
PatchEnvelope.description: `{ok: true, patch: {...}}` for `POST /patches/{patch_id}/withdraw`, plus what the withdrawal did to the observations the patch answered. **Not shared with the filing route** -- its description said so until 2026-08-24 and that was already false: `POST /patches` has its own `DraftEnvelope`, because a field one of two callers cannot produce is indistinguishable from a field nobody serves. The two shapes are mirror images: drafting reports `addressed` / `not_addressed`, withdrawing reports `reopened` / `not_reopened`.

reopened.description: Observation ids this withdrawal returned to `triaged`. Drafting is the only producer of `addressed`; withdrawing the last live patch is what undoes it. A row that stays `addressed` because a second draft is still open is in `not_reopened`, not here.

not_reopened.description: Observations the withdrawn patch was attached to and that were **not** returned, each with the state it is in and why. Only an `addressed` row is a candidate: `open -> triaged` is also a declared edge, so returning every attached row would triage one nobody has looked at. A terminal row (`declined`, `duplicate`) lands here too.

PatchListResponse.title: PatchListResponse
PatchListResponse.description: Patches **newest first**, where the observation queue is oldest-first. The asymmetry is the point: an observation queue is work waiting, so the row that has waited longest is next; a patch list is work done, so the one just authored is the one being looked for.

DraftEnvelope.title: DraftEnvelope
DraftEnvelope.description: `POST /patches` only. `PatchEnvelope` plus what drafting did to the observations the patch answers. Its own schema rather than two optional fields on `PatchEnvelope`, which is the withdraw response and reports the mirror-image pair under different names: a field declared on a shape that one of its two callers cannot produce is indistinguishable from a field nobody serves.

addressed.description: Observation ids this draft moved to `addressed`. Drafting is the producer of that state; nothing else sets it.

not_addressed.description: Observations the patch attached to and could **not** move, each with the state it is in and the store's refusal. `-> addressed` is declared only from `triaged` and `blocked_on_a_person`, so drafting against an `open` row attaches the patch and leaves the row where it is. Reported rather than refused, because refusing would break the steward's actual sequence — read the queue, draft — and silence would make a row that did not move look like one that did.
